caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Home Depot U.S.A., Inc.
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — prior September 8 San Joaquin packet was never filed and is superseded as filing strategy. New E.D. Cal. review draft uses FCRA as the federal-question anchor and is conditioned on the Home Depot-specific First Advantage report and a verified discovery date.
note: The September 8, 2026 San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Federal review draft lives at internal/docs/matter-37/EDCA_FEDERAL_COMPLAINT_REVIEW_DRAFT.md. Do not file until every report placeholder is filled from Home Depot's own First Advantage report and the FCRA/ICRAA discovery date is verified. First Advantage is treated as the nonparty CRA unless its Home Depot-specific records support an independent vendor claim.
defendants: Home Depot U.S.A., Inc. is the proposed sole opening defendant as employer/user of the report. First Advantage is identified as the consumer reporting agency and a discovery source, not yet a defendant. Confirm the exact Home Depot ordering/user entity from the Home Depot-specific report and onboarding records before filing.
causes: [FEDERAL ANCHOR] FCRA, 15 U.S.C. § 1681b(b)(3)(A) — Home Depot allegedly took adverse employment action based in whole or in part on the First Advantage report without first providing the report and written Summary of Rights; negligent/willful remedies under §§ 1681o/1681n.

[DISTINCT STATE OMISSION] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — upon denying/ending employment under circumstances in which an investigative report was obtained, Home Depot allegedly failed to advise Plaintiff and supply the CRA name/address. Pleaded as a different omission from the FCRA pre-adverse failure to avoid § 1786.52(a) same-act duplication.

[REPORT-CONDITIONED] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — strongest version requires Home Depot-specific First Advantage report to identify California-registry-sourced information and show Home Depot used the report for the Tracy employment decision.
[OMITTED] UCL — limited remedial upside and unnecessary federal standing/remedy side fight.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — reserve unless the actual Home Depot product is an ordinary consumer credit report rather than an investigative employment report.
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED — approximate August 2024 adverse-action date creates facial two-year limitations problems.
[RESERVED] FCRA § 1681b(b)(2)(A), Fair Chance Act / FEHA, and First Advantage vendor claims — add only if the actual forms, exhaustion record, or CRA conduct support them.
key_facts: Plaintiff states that Home Depot hired him for the Tracy distribution/fulfillment operation at 5395 Hopkins Road, he accepted and began onboarding, Home Depot ran an employment background check, and the employment then stopped. Federal redraft assumes First Advantage is Home Depot's CRA but does not import facts from UPS/FedEx or other employers. The filing version must insert the Home Depot-specific report completion date, exact client/requestor name, component results, registry source language, adjudication/client criterion, and adverse-action date. It must also plead the true date and event by which Plaintiff discovered the FCRA/ICRAA violations; the 2024 ghosting alone disclosed the employment result, not necessarily the report-based statutory violations.
procedural_status: Pre-filing federal redraft on branch matter37-edca-federal-redraft. Prior signed San Joaquin complaint/intake dated September 8, 2026 were never filed and should not be treated as operative. Proposed forum is E.D. Cal., Sacramento, based on federal-question jurisdiction under the FCRA plus supplemental California claims. Review draft intentionally omits UCL, CCRAA, Tameny/IIED, prospective injunction theories, and a redundant FCRA § 1681m(a) count. Filing gates: Home Depot-specific First Advantage report, exact discovery date, confirmation the Tracy job is outside the DOT remote-application exception, and correct Home Depot legal entity.
damages: Federal draft seeks nonduplicative actual/compensatory damages including lost employment compensation; FCRA remedies under §§ 1681n/1681o; ICRAA actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater, plus punitive damages if the statutory showing is met; and remedies authorized by Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A). No wage rate or duration is presently fixed in the record. No civil-penalty-only valuation is assumed.
risk: Main filing risk is limitations: alleged adverse action is around August 2024, so the complaint needs the true later discovery date for FCRA § 1681p and ICRAA § 1786.52. Merits strength then turns on the Home Depot-specific report. A source field naming the California registry plus an adverse/decisional component materially strengthens § 290.46; a court-record source with no California-registry sourcing materially weakens it. Do not file with borrowed First Advantage facts from other matters.
evidence: Plaintiff's statement — accepted Home Depot Tracy hire/onboarding; employment background check; employment then stopped
Home Depot-specific First Advantage report — REQUIRED filing exhibit/source; exact fields must be inserted before filing
E.D. Cal. Local Rule 120(d) — San Joaquin County civil actions commence on the Sacramento side
EDCA federal complaint review draft and redraft notes under internal/docs/matter-37/
